original_value: Autonomous vehicle platoon is a promising paradigm towards traffic congestion problems in the intelligent transportation system. However, under certain circumstances, the advantage of the platoon cannot be fully developed. In this paper, we focus on the highway Electronic Toll Collection (ETC) charging problem. We try to let the opportunistic platoon pass the ETC as a whole. There are three main issues in this scenario. Firstly, the opportunistic platoon is temporarily composed; vehicles do not trust each other. Secondly, single vehicle may try to escape from the ETC charging by following the platoon. Finally, platoon members may collude with each other and try to underreport the number of vehicles in the platoon so as to evade payment. To solve these challenges, we propose a blockchain-based efficient highway toll paradigm for the opportunistic platoon. The driving history, credential information of every registered vehicle, is recorded and verified from the blockchain. A roadside unit (RSU) is adopted to distinguish the single vehicle from the platoon and in charge of lane allocation. Additionally, an aggregate signature is introduced to accelerate the authentication procedure in the RSU. We analyse the potential security threats in this scenario. The experimental result indicates that our scheme is efficient and practical.

result.paraphrase: Autonomous vehicle platooning is a promising approach to addressing traffic congestion in intelligent transportation systems. However, in some cases, its benefits cannot be fully realized. This paper examines the highway Electronic Toll Collection (ETC) charging problem and aims to allow an opportunistic platoon to pass through ETC as a whole. Three main issues arise in this setting. First, the opportunistic platoon is formed temporarily, so vehicles do not trust one another. Second, a single vehicle may attempt to evade ETC charges by following the platoon. Third, platoon members may collude to underreport the number of vehicles in the platoon in order to avoid payment. To address these challenges, we propose a blockchain-based efficient highway toll scheme for opportunistic platoons. The driving history and credential information of each registered vehicle are stored and verified on the blockchain. A roadside unit (RSU) is used to distinguish single vehicles from platoons and to handle lane allocation. In addition, an aggregate signature is introduced to speed up authentication at the RSU. We analyze the possible security threats in this scenario. Experimental results show that the proposed scheme is efficient and practical.
